title: Share control
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Can you share control, or do you need to hold it?

Jose said that the brother told the person in the book: you don't know how to be on the board of a company. What I took from it is that he doesn't think he can share control. He's not the kind of person who shares control easily.

Jose said that if you want to put a board of directors together, it is a very complex situation but very necessary. He told of a famous founder who had a board, and it ended up not fitting his strategy, and he was fired by his own board, because at twenty-five he did not know how to get along with people.

A student said: you're unable to take other people's opinions into consideration, so you rule like a dictator: my way or the highway. There is also a risk of bias if you don't have a board. I don't really like a board of directors, but I like a board of advisors in an early start-up, for when you are drinking the Kool-Aid.
Jose said: it is very important that people see you are surrounded by people with experience in the industry.
Where do you refuse to share control, and what does that cost you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where you won't share control.
Write what it has cost you.
Write the advice you have ignored.
Write who could tell you what you don't want to hear.
Write one decision you will share this month.

check.q: What did Jose take from the brother's remark?
choices: The person doesn't share control easily

check.q: What did a student say about not taking others' opinions?
choices: You rule like a dictator and risk bias

check.q: What did a student prefer in an early start-up?

recap: Know where you won't share control. Keep advisors who can tell you the truth.
